newsitem.title: USA: One in three Americans don't save - survey.
newsitem.headline: One in three Americans don't save - survey.

text.p: One-third of Americans spend their paychecks before they get them, according to a survey released Thursday by Quicken Financial Network, the personal finance Web site of software maker Intuit Inc.

The survey, possibly the first via the Internet, found that 32 percent of 7,210 respondents have simply stopped saving altogether. Twenty percent routinely get overdue notices from creditors, 17 percent don't have enough money to pay their taxes, and 10 percent ask family, friends or colleagues for loans.
Four percent of the respondents were among the more than 1 million Americans who filed for personal bankruptcy last year, a 25 percent rise from the total in 1995, Quicken said.

"Despite their awareness of the issue, however, many Americans are struggling to break what has become an uncontrollable cycle of spending beyond their means," said Nancy Dunnan, a personal finance writer and columnist for Money Talks, an Internet-based magazine.

"For me, the most alarming finding was that one-third have stopped saving altogether and, perhaps, given up hope. That tells me they feel discouraged and out of control, and believe that saving even $10 a week just won't put a dent in their debt."

The 12-question survey also found that 6 percent of Americans don't know their total credit card debt, 10 percent don't know their total monthly payments, 14 percent don't know the interest rate on their credit cards and 9 percent get cash advances from one credit card to pay off debt on another card.
Nine percent post-date personal checks so they won't bounce and 6 percent borrow for regular, everyday essentials such as groceries, clothing and gasoline for their car.

Most of the respondents (49 percent) were aged 33 to 49 years, and 42 percent had household income ranging from $26,000 to $40,000 per year. Eighty-one percent of respondents were male. Eighteen percent owned their own business.

The survey was undertaken to determine why so many Americans are falling into debt. The poll was conducted simultaneously on Quicken's Web sites: www.quicken.com and www.talks.com, from April 30th through May 16th.
At the same time, Quicken Financial Network introduced its free Debt Reduction Planner that people could link to straight from the survey.
